elements.markdown: The server takes **900 ms**, including **620 ms in repeated per-account queries**. Rendering the **2,000-row table takes another 350 ms**. We can work on SQL and the frontend together. Billing must be fresh after edits, search must cover every row, and the proposals below use existing infrastructure.

elements.multi: Which improvements should we explore together?

options.description: Establish how the database executes the queries before choosing a SQL change.
Replace repeated queries with set-based SQL; promising for the 620 ms hotspot, but verify the plan and results.
Reduce browser work while retaining all rows in search; changes how users navigate the table.

Batch per-account queries.text: Compare the current queries with a batched version and check billing correctness after edits. No delayed billing cache.

Batch per-account queries.check: Also explore reusing summary results for up to 30 seconds

reveals.text: This can reduce repeated summary work using existing infrastructure, at the cost of briefly stale reporting. Keep it separate from billing reads and check refresh behavior after edits.

Render fewer table rows.select: Which table approach should we compare?

options.description: Render one page at a time; simpler navigation, but users must move between pages.
Render the visible window while preserving continuous scrolling; requires careful keyboard and accessibility checks.
Assess navigation and rendering costs before committing to a table design.

reveals.text: Search will run across the full dataset before pagination or virtualization. Compare keyboard navigation and access to all rows as well as rendering time.

elements.select: What should the next step produce?

options.description: Inspect the selected areas and compare options before changing behavior.
Try the selected SQL and frontend changes after baseline and query-plan checks; verify freshness, full-data search, and navigation.
